research_question: Is a lower student-teacher ratio associated with higher academic performance?

ivs.description: Student-teacher ratio (constructed as students divided by teachers) — the main predictor of interest representing classroom size/teacher availability.

dv.description: Academic performance measured as the average standardized test score (constructed from reading and math scores).

controls.description: District average income (in USD 1,000) used as a socioeconomic control.
Percent qualifying for reduced-price lunch, used as a proxy for student socioeconomic status.
Percent of English learners (students for whom English is a second language), used as a demographic control.
Expenditure per student, used as a control for school funding/resources.

extracted_analysis.analysis_code:
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv("caschools.csv")

# Student-teacher ratio
df["str"] = df["students"] / df["teachers"]

# Academic performance: average of read and math
df["avg_score"] = df[["read", "math"]].mean(axis=1)

# Simple correlation
corr = df["str"].corr(df["avg_score"])

# Simple OLS
X_simple = sm.add_constant(df["str"])
model_simple = sm.OLS(df["avg_score"], X_simple).fit()

# OLS with common controls
controls = ["income", "lunch", "english", "expenditure"]
X_ctrl = sm.add_constant(df[["str"] + controls])
model_ctrl = sm.OLS(df["avg_score"], X_ctrl).fit()

# Save summary stats to stdout for inspection
print("Correlation (STR vs avg_score):", corr)
print("\nSimple OLS:")
print(model_simple.summary())
print("\nControlled OLS:")
print(model_ctrl.summary())
